headline: Committee approved its mission statement and heard updates on immigration policy, housing complaints, and police chief hiring
summary: The REIB committee approved a revised mission and purpose statement after feedback from prior meetings. It heard a presentation from Erin Jacobsen of the Vermont Asylum Assistance Project on state immigration legislation, received office updates on Trusted Community Voices hiring and staff departures, and got an update on the Police Chief search, which aims for a September announcement.
decisions: Approved the agenda and minutes unanimously

decision_evidence.quote: Councilor Grant moved to approve the agenda and the minutes and Councilor Carpenter seconded. The motion passed unanimously.

• Call to Order 
o Meeting Called to order at 5:40 pm 
• Approve Agenda & Minutes 
o Councilor Grant moved to approve the agenda and the minutes and Councilor Carpenter seconded. The 
motion passed unanimously. 
• Public Forum 
o Richard Hilliard spoke about recent federal immigration policy changes regarding adjustment of 
immigration status. He shared his own experience and expressed concern over reports that many 
individuals may now be required to complete immigration processing outside the United States.  
▪ He noted that many affected individuals come from countries without U.S. embassies or 
consulates, creating significant barriers. 
▪ Encouraged the committee to consider both the humanitarian impacts and potential municipal 
planning implications for Burlington. 
• Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson acknowledge growing uncertainty among immigrants, visa 
holders, and green card holders due to changing federal immigration policies. She noted 
that the scheduled presentation from the Vermont Asylum Assistance Project would 
provide additional context later in the meeting. 
o  Alexander, a Burlington resident, father, first-generation American, and longtime human services 
worker, shared concerns regarding unsafe housing conditions. 
▪ He described ongoing construction at his rental property that has disrupted daily life and 
created unsafe living conditions. He reported working with City inspectors, tenant organization, 
Legal Aid, and other agencies but felt he had been repeatedly referred between organizations 
without resolution. 
▪ He shared that the property had been declared unfit for human habitation and expressed 
concern about retaliation from contractors after reporting code violations. 
▪ He discussed the emotional and financial toll the situation has placed on his family and highlight 
broader concerns about housing insecurity. 
• Councilor Grant offered to work directly with the resident and requested follow-up 
information regarding the property and landlord. 
• Councilor Grant committed to contacting Permitting and Inspections to better 
understand the situation and identify possible protections. 
• Committee housing concerns affect many Burlington residents. 
o Loan Nguyen shared a citizenship issue a community member is having with the Department of 
Homeland of Security. She expressed the community member is afraid to leave their house due to the 
current enforcement. 
▪ Erin Jacobsen directed Loan to the Vermont Asylum Assistance Project’s website to submit a 
legal help request and mentioned some upcoming naturalization clinics being planned. 
▪ Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson noted the need for a more streamlined and accessible way for 
community members to find resources and reach the right support. She noted the Trusted 
Community Voices program (TCVs) plays a key role in bridging community members to these 
resources.
• REIB Office Updates 
o Director Kelli Perkins shared updates on REIB initiatives and ongoing work since the committee’s 
previous meeting.  
▪ She informed everyone that two Trusted Community Voices liaison positions are currently 
posted on the city website: one for the Spanish-speaking community, one for the Bosnian 
community. Interviews are scheduled for early August. 
▪ Katie Greene departed July 9th to work with the State of Vermont.  
• Due to a 45-day posting restriction in the passed budget, the Community and Belonging 
Manager role cannot be posted until end of August.  
▪ Director Perkins let everyone know nearly all proposed slate of appointees for the Aging Council, 
except a representative for the New American community 
▪ Christian Berry added the Language Access policy and procedure are being revised and the 
implementation plan is being mapped out but an assessment will need to be started across the 
city.  
• A culture survey has been administered to city employees. Executive summary is being 
developed and will be ready to be shared out in early August. 
o Councilor Grant flagged that COTS is planning a Back-to-School Bonanza and recommended outreach to 
Mr. Hartnett and his foundation about possible funding support for a second event closer to the start of 
school. 
▪ Christian Berry noted that the Back-to-School supply event was a TCV originated idea last year 
and that there is some IDEAL grant funding remaining. A meeting with the mayor on August 4th 
will include a discussion about funding and resourcing. Any additional funding sources would be 
welcome. 
• Committee Mission Statement & Meeting Agreements (action to approve) 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson presented the third and final revision of the committee’s mission and 
purpose statement, incorporating feedback from the June and prior meetings. Refer to the video. 
• State-Level Immigration Policy Updates and Local Implementation Planning (Guest Erin Jacobsen, Vermont 
Asylum Assistance Project) 
o Erin Jacobsen presented on immigrant rights victories from the 2026 Vermont legislative session and 
priorities for the upcoming 2027 session (beginning January 2027). Refer to the video. 
▪ The presentation included information on recent state legislation intended to strengthen 
protections for immigrant communities, guidance on responding to immigration enforcement, 
providing resources for immigrant families, asylum seekers, and service providers. 
▪ She shared they are developing informational guidance documents to help agencies implement 
new legal requirements. 
▪ Tiffanie Katsuva and Maryan Maalin expressed the importance of presenting directly to refugee 
and immigrant communities with interpretation. 
• Erin Jacobsen agreed. 
▪ Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson voiced the REIB’s continued commitment to serving as a source for 
community engagement on these topics and will explore opportunities to co-host forums. 
• Police Chief Hiring Process Update 
o Councilor Grant provided updates on the national search for Burlington’s next Police Chief. 
▪ The hiring process remains on schedule and the International Association of Chiefs of Police 
(IACP) is assisting with recruitment and candidate screening. 
▪ Community engagement informed the recruitment profile, including stakeholder meetings and a 
public survey with more than 600 responses. 
• Committee members requested additional analysis of survey responses from younger 
residents to better understand youth perspectives.
▪ Fifteen applications were received, with four candidates advancing to the interview stage. 
Interviews began during the week of the meeting. 
▪ Candidates are responding to standardized interview questions and completing a written 
scenario exercise. 
▪ The committee is evaluating candidates based on leadership experience, commitment to 
community engagement, and ability to balance departmental leadership with community needs. 
▪ Finalists will be forwarded to the mayor for additional interviews and background checks. 
▪ The goal is to announce a new Police Chief by September to allow for an overlap and transition 
period with Chief Burke before his departure. 
▪ Recruitment materials, committee membership, and the hiring timeline remain publicly 
available. 
• Aging Council Update 
o Director Perkins noted that the updates regarding the Aging Council had already been provided during 
the REIB Office Updates. 
• Adjournment 
o The meeting adjourned at 7:07 p.m.
